summary: Instagram is where nearly all your audience is: most Hindi videos get 1,000+ views there, while YouTube Shorts mostly get under 30 views. The best videos are about robots or sensors that 'do something surprising' (gyro robot, clap switch, line follower) and they earn the most likes and saves. Generic 'how does X work?' videos about everyday items (smoke detector, lift, tap, mall door) get low views and almost no engagement.
winningPattern: Short, punchy Hindi titles about a robot or maker-project sensor with a surprising or contradictory claim ('Gyro ke bina robot gir jaata', 'Clap switch taali nahi, shor sunta hai', 'Line follower ke paas dimaag nahi hota'). Visual demo of a robot or Arduino-style build, shown on Instagram Reels first. Newest posts (Oct 29 to Nov 2) do best, suggesting the robot/maker angle is gaining momentum.
doMore: Make robot and maker-project videos (balancing, line follower, obstacle avoidance, sound or light triggered switches)
Open with a bold 'X ke bina Y nahi hota' or 'X nahi, Y karta hai' claim that flips what viewers expect
Show a physical build failing or working on screen in the first 2 seconds to boost saves and shares
Post to Instagram first and treat it as the main platform; reuse the same clip on YouTube with a sharper title
End with a clear save-worthy takeaway (a pin diagram or one-line rule) since saves are your strongest signal
stopDoing: Generic 'Kaise kaam karta hai? 🤔' titles on everyday items like taps, lifts, smoke alarms and mall doors
Making several near-duplicate videos on the same topic (two smoke detector, two automatic tap, two IR sensor videos)
Posting English-titled videos when the audience is responding to Hindi
